thread:
jordan: Repro + profiling for KV cache memory growth when continuous batching merges long-context requests. I reproduced a steady memory climb and intermittent stalls when batches try to merge and inherit large KV footprints. Posting steps + quick flamegraph snapshot.

jordan: Repro steps (dev laptop, docker):
```bash
# generate long-context traffic with mixed lengths
python scripts/bench_kv.py --clients 40 --seq-dist long_tail --kv-reuse 0.6 --duration 10m
# run the service with kvcache debug logging
RUNTIME_DEBUG=kvcache ./bin/redwood-runtime --config test/kv-batch-config.yaml
```
Log snippet from the run: 
```
[kvcache] admit batch merge request id=4823 ctx_len=8192 kv_slots=4096 -> merge_wait
[kvcache] merge_wait: head=0 tail=3 duration_ms=1324 blocking_slot=2987
[memory] rss_growth_mb +56
[kvcache] eviction_trigger shard=1 scanned=64 reclaimed=0
```

meera: Nice, that matches the small repro I saw on staging. Can you attach the flamegraph + perf counters? :eyes:

jordan: Uploaded pprof/flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/pprof/2234567890/kv-merge.svg
Top symbols: 
- kv_merge_wait_loop ~ 43%
- kv_frag_coalesce ~ 18%
- memcpy (large) ~ 12%
- scheduler::park / futex_wait ~ 7%
Also saw a surprising amount of time in the mem allocator during merge window.

sam: Hmm. Two quick hypotheses: 1) merging batches pulls KV pages from many different contexts causing page churn and allocator pressure, 2) kernel choice for large matmul / attention leads to high temporary allocations that bloat the RSS during merge.

raj: I ran an A/B with cross-batch merge disabled (merge_threshold=0) on a small fleet: p50 ~ unchanged, p95 went down 30ms, but p99 increased for some long-req flows since they lost batching benefits. Memory growth stopped in that window.

jordan: Good datapoint. So merging helps latency for common cases but creates high variance and memory tail. I also captured a slab profile: most long-lived allocations during merge are KV page pin lists and a few large per-request buffers.

meera: Can we try two mitigation experiments: a) age-based merge: only allow merge if both batch heads have KV age < X; b) limit merged KV footprint by rejecting merges that would exceed per-batch kv_slot_budget.

sam: I sketched a patch for (b): quick heuristic in batch_merger.cc:
```c++
if (merged_kv_slots > config.kv_slot_budget) {
  reject_merge(); // keep as separate batches
}
```
On a short run this cut peak RSS by ~20% and reduced merge_wait tail. Not a full fix but promising.

jordan: Also tried tuning kernel selection: forcing the attention kernel to the streaming-friendly path reduced peak temp allocations ~8% in perf runs. That indicates kernel selection + merge heuristics interplay.

perf-bot: perf alert: service/encode p99 latency increased from 210ms to 295ms at 2234567893 (detected by nightly smoke).

raj: We should be careful with wholesale disabling merges because throughput suffers. Proposal: implement a conservative merge gate that uses both kv_slot_budget and an estimated extra_rss cost metric derived from recent allocations. If est_extra_rss > threshold -> reject merge.

meera: For implementation we need: signal for per-batch kv footprint, fast estimator for extra_rss (maybe a moving window of recent merge delta), and tests that simulate long contexts. I can pick this up next sprint.

jordan: I added a minimal repro test to our perf harness: bench/kv_longctx_merge_test.py. It asserts no RSS growth > 30MB over 5 minutes with merge enabled. Failing CI gives trace to the pprof link.

sam: One more observation from the flamegraph: kv_frag_coalesce spends nontrivial time scanning many fragments with tiny reclaim yields. Possibly fragmentation makes eviction scan expensive during merge. Consider adding a fast-path that pre-checks fragment reclamation potential before accepting merge.

meera: Agreed. I'll add a lightweight fragment-sample API that returns estimated reclaimable_ratio quickly and gate merges on that.

jordan: TL;DR action items:
- meera: prototype reclaim-sampler + age-based merge gate (PR next week)
- sam: land kv_slot_budget reject heuristic as config-guarded change (small rollback risk)
- raj: run scaled A/B with conservative merge gate once meera's sampler is in
- jordan: extend perf harness with release-mode longctx merge test and hook to perf-bot alerts

raj: ack. Also added a note to the incident board in case we see regressions during rollout.

sam: Good. If anyone wants the raw perf captures let me know and I'll drop the pcap + perf.data.

jordan: Thanks all. We'll iterate on merge gating + kernel hints. Expect smaller change PRs this week. :thumbsup:
